profile.reading:
This point is mapped as "Vantage San Antonio I" at 5207 Rogers Road, San Antonio, TX, in the Westover Hills area; research this session found no standalone Vantage building actually named "San Antonio I" or "TX1" on Vantage's own site or in any secondary source (Data Center Dynamics, Baxtel, DataCenterHawk). "TX1" instead appears to function as an informal umbrella label for Vantage's Texas Research Park sub-campus (Omicron Drive, home to TX11 and TX12) in some third-party materials, while the Rogers Road address this point carries actually matches Vantage's separate Westover Hills sub-campus (home to TX21 and TX22, both individually tracked elsewhere in this registry). Given this naming ambiguity, this entry does not assert this point represents a sixth, independently confirmed San Antonio building; it most likely duplicates or mis-labels one of the four already-documented San Antonio buildings (TX11, TX12, TX21, TX22) rather than representing new capacity.

Vantage acquired 57.9 acres on Omicron/Theta Drive from the University of Texas System Board of Regents in July 2023, and a separate 31 acres at State Highway 151/Wiseman Boulevard in August 2023, together forming its San Antonio campus. This San Antonio campus is distinct from Vantage's much larger "Frontier" mega-campus, a separate $25 billion, 1.4-gigawatt development in rural Shackelford County, Texas, announced in August 2025.

The broader San Antonio data center corridor Vantage operates within has grown alongside CPS Energy's dedicated large-load substation investments and Bexar County's property-tax abatement agreements aimed at diversifying the local economy beyond military and tourism employment. Because no single confirmed building at this location could be matched to a specific Vantage-published facility name, address, or specification sheet, this entry should be read as a documented ambiguity pending a Bexar County Appraisal District parcel lookup rather than as a confirmed independent Vantage facility distinct from the four already-identified San Antonio buildings (TX11, TX12, TX21, TX22) in this dataset. CPS Energy's integrated resource plan and Texas's ERCOT grid operator have both cited data centers as a fast-growing large-load category driving new transmission and generation investment across the San Antonio region through the early 2030s.

reading.body:
This entry is not a publishable facility record. The operator has not confirmed a building-specific megawatt figure or distinct street address for Vantage San Antonio I. The registry places it within 150 meters of two other rows, TX11 and TX12, which share the same Texas Research Park campus in Bexar County near the Omicron and Theta Drive crossing. A 2023 local report documented Vantage's purchase of 57.9 acres at this location, but the correspondence between the legacy name "San Antonio I" and the operator's current building designations remains unconfirmed.

Without a published capacity figure, this facility cannot be ranked among Texas's 18 data centers with disclosed megawatt counts. The state hosts 133 mapped facilities in total, of which 468 MW is publicly specified. This row's capacity, if distinct from TX11 and TX12, is not among those published figures.

Readers evaluating Texas AI infrastructure should refer to facilities with operator-confirmed capacity and addresses. The campus assets at Texas Research Park may matter to regional AI build-out, but this specific row contributes no new data to that assessment until the operator publishes building-level specifications.
